---
title: "phplyr"
subtitle: "A PHP port of the Tidyverse's dplyr and tidyr."
---

Filter, transform, join, and reshape tables with dplyr- and tidyr-style
functions. Use PHP 8.5 pipes, or method chains on PHP 8.3 and later.

## A first pipeline

Keep the students who studied at least five hours, summarize each school, and
print the five schools with the highest average score.

```bash
composer require phpstats/phplyr
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/phplyr/{{< var release >}}/docs/data/schools.csv
```

{{< include examples/_first-pipeline.md >}}

## phplyr and phibble

The tables come from [phibble](https://github.com/phpstats/phibble), which
Composer installs with phplyr. phplyr adds dplyr's and tidyr's functions on
top of phibble's table methods, so a pipeline runs on an in-memory
`DataFrame`, on a database table as SQL, or on Polars.

phplyr has:

- dplyr's single-table and two-table functions, with grouped window
  functions, `across()`, column selectors, and `join_by()` conditions.
- tidyr's pivoting, completing, splitting, nesting, and list-column functions.
- janitor's `clean_names()`, `remove_empty()`, `get_dupes()`, and `tabyl()`.
- `lm()`, `glm()`, `lmer()`, and `glmer()`, which fit models with phit.

[Functions and methods](reference/index.qmd) lists every function and
method, with a link to its reference entry.

## Install

```bash
composer require phpstats/phplyr
```

phplyr needs PHP 8.3 or later with the mbstring and PDO extensions.
[Installation](getting-started.qmd#installation) lists the optional
extensions, and [Compatibility and limitations](compatibility.qmd) lists the
dplyr features phplyr doesn't have.
